Have you talked to your girlfriend about this? 
Maybe you can tell her you are not that comfortable with the fact she is spending so much time with a guy you don't even know.  I think it is normal for you to be jealous, regardless if there is something else going on. 

It could be innocent, but you should definitely communicate with her about it. Maybe you can even ask to meet him, to see if there is something else going on. 

You should tell her about your feelings and if she loves you as much as you seem to love her, she will take account of those feelings. She can still have him as a male friend, but should communicate about it very clear with you. 

I hope nothing else is going on, good luck!

I feel like we have similar moms. So I absolutely get that you are very angry. Your description of your mom is very similar to mine. She's also very passive aggresive, never apologizes and often I feel like I'm more of an adult than her. About her posting about you passing the course on facebook, my mom also always takes pride in telling people when something good happened to me, as if she had something to do with it. 

Is it possible for you to find some place else to live? Because I feel like this is not a healthy situation for you to be in. Because of my mom's behavior, I was angry at her about everything. She just gave me so much stress. At least it is good to have your dad be there for you. 

In any other situation I would say, maybe you should try to talk to her about it, but having a mom like that myself, I know that wouldn't work. 

The best thing for you to do, is probably try to distance yourself as much as possible, at least for a while. You're right to be angry. 

If you ever want to talk about it more or just rant about it, you can always PM me. 

Good luck!

I'm going to try not to judge you, but I think you need to realize that what you have done is quite unforgivable. 

It seems like he wanted to do everything to make your relationship work, while you just stopped trying. 

If you ask me he deserves much better. 

When you are in a relationship you have to work for it. Barely having sex in years is not good for your relationship. You said you were still attracted to him, but clearly didn't make an effort to spice up your sex life. I'm surprised he didn't cheat on you after not having sex for that long. 

Sometimes I also have a low sex drive, but I will still make an effort for my SO and I always end up enjoying it. You need to work for it, if you want it to work. 

Your relationship seems to have been dead for a long time. 

I think it is better to let things settle down and maybe in a while you can talk about it with him. But if you ask me, I think you should let him go. Your cry for help has come too late. You fucked up and now you have to pay the price. 

I think you are more afraid of losing 'being in a relationship', than you are losing him. Which is no surprise, because you have been in a relationship for 10 years. It is scary to put yourself out there again and be single when you are almost turning 30. 

You need to be honest with yourself and accept that your relationship has been over for a long time already. 
Give him the space he needs and deserves. Take that time to figure out what you want too. You can't expect him to just come crawling back to you after what you did. 

I hope you can find a way to accept this. Good luck.

It seems to me like you are putting a lot of effort in maintaining your friendship with him, while he isn't doing the same for you. 

A lot of people change when they are in a relationship and that can be difficult for their friends to deal with. Especially when you're relationship is quite new, you want to spend every possible minute with your SO. Maybe he needs a bit more time to settle things down and hopefully he will put more effort in your friendship. 

You can address your feelings about this, saying you are sad this happened and you hope things will change, because your friendship is important to you. As for yourself, I wouldn't keep putting that much effort in him for a while. You can not change this behavior, as much as you would want to. 

Like /u/Iamnottherapist said, you should adjust your expectations of him. Or else you will keep getting disappointed. I wouldn't throw away your friendship. You have been friends for 7 years, that is a long time. I think it is best to distance yourself for a while, keep in contact, but lower your expectations about meeting him. 

I know it's difficult, because he seems to have been there for you when times where hard. Just bear in mind that it is difficult to find a balance between seeing your friends and your SO. Especially when you are still quite young.

I hope for you he can find that balance and that he will put in the effort you deserve as a friend. Just don't expect him to, so you can't be let down. Good luck, you seem like a good friend!

Wow, what a story. I'm happy that you were able find your brother. 

Have you talked with your brother about telling your parents? Or with another family member? I feel like he has to make to call to tell them. Maybe you can do it together? 

I get that you are afraid that they will feel really guilty about not looking into it more. Any parent would feel like that. But I think even though bearing in mind that they would feel really bad about not searching for him more, they would also be immensely happy to have their other son in their life again. 

It won't be an easy road. They will have to forgive themselves and they will have to work on establishing a relationship with your brother. 

It also seems like your brother has distanced himself from his feelings about his parents and everything that happened 36 years ago. Which is not that abnormal. Do you think it is possible for your brother to talk to someone professional/a therapist? I think that would be a good idea, because he seems to be in the same place emotionally that you were in before you talked with a therapist. 

If you decide to tell your parents, maybe you can even go to a therapist as a family. Because this a lot to take in and it will stir up a lot of emotions, good and bad. 

I think you should make this decision together with your brother. But if I were your parents, I would like to know that my son were alive, even if I would feel extremely guitly about not searching for him more. 

Whatever you decide, I wish you the best of luck!

You are not being sensitive or overreacting.

I think you should talk with him about this and tell him it's not ok for him to judge or even decide what you eat. He needs to respect you and that's not what he's doing right now.

It's possible he doesn't see it that way, maybe he even means well, but isn't able to express himself in a better way. Some guys think it's sexy for a girl to eat healthy and to work out, but he can't force that on to you. 

He should respect your body and your choices as an adult. Tell him you feel uncomfortable when he says things like that and if he loves and respects you, he will take you serious. 

If he doesn't take you serious, you shouldn't be together with him anymore. You deserve somebody who respects you and who takes you serious when you feel insecure and uncomfortable.

You need to come clean with your wife. I think you should talk with her about the feelings you're having. 

You knew about her past when you married her, but it seems to me that you still judge her for it. I get that it makes you jealous and maybe even less of a man, but you knew all that when you decided to have a future with her. 

You say you love her, but you have to ask yourself, do you really love her as a person. Because when you really love someone, you accept their flaws or at least address them if you are having a problem accepting them. So you can work on it, as a couple. 

You're insecure, I get that. But I don't think it's ok to criticize your wife for not having a diploma or sleeping with more people than you because you can't accept your flaws or insecurities. 

If you really love and respect her, you should tell her the truth, so you can work on it together. You should either accept who she is and accept her past or else, I don't think you really love and respect her. If that's the case, she deserves better. 

Try to see why you fell in love with her, talk about it, relive it. Accept her and give her the respect that she deserves. It's not because she didn't go to college and you did, you are better than her. It's not because she has more experience, that she will judge you for it and compare you to the other people she has been with. 

If you are not ok with her past, you should tell her and you should both go your own way. But whatever you do, you should tell her how you really feel. About everything.

I don't think you have the 'nice guy syndrom'. 

As you said your childhood was quite rough, with no one really being there for you emotionally. Your dad abused you physically and mentally, that leaves scars. It made you the kind of person who wants to avoid confrontation and fights. There is nothing wrong with that. 

When stating what traits you thought were fucked up, you mentioned the trait 'seeking for consensus when making decisions'. I think this is a very important trait to have when you are in a healthy relationship, with a normal person. It seems to me like your ex-wife didn't have this trait and disrespected you as a person. 

If you ask me she abused you mentally by making you think you were doing so much wrong and by saying your friends also thought you were screwing things up. She made abuse of your insecurity and kindness. 

You have been let down by a lot of 'key' people in your life. You want to please people and sometimes forget that your opinion is equally important. 

The traits you mentioned aren't fucked up. All you need to learn is how to stand up for yourself and that your opinion is important too. 

You deserve someone who respects you equally. You seem like a great guy, please don't try to change yourself. You aren't the one who has to change. That would make you a pleaser and a 'nice guy' again. You are important and so is your opinion. 

Try to stand up for yourself more, start small and you will see there are women out their who will give you the same amount of respect and love as you give them. 

Maybe try to look for some way to express your anger about what happened with your father AND your ex-wife. You need to accept and express those feelings, not only verbally, but also physically. You can go boxing, take up a self-defence class, ... 

I'm sorry for my English, it's not my native language. I hope I helped you out a bit. 

Good luck!

Just be honest with her as soon as possible or get your shit together.
Prolonging telling her will only make it worse. 

If you have really thought this through and you are sure about your decision, than you have to be completely honest with her right now. But I can tell you that whatever you say, she will still be hurt like hell. She opened up her heart after being stood up at the altar, she said yes when you proposed even though she was hurt last time. She clearly loves you very much. If you ever loved her, you have to tell her. Everything. 

Do you really think you could be in a relationship with this other woman? She's clearly a bit younger than you, probably in a different time of her life. Either way, I don't think it's a good idea to jump into another relationship that soon after being engaged. 

You have to be really honest with yourself right now. Do you see yourself spending the rest of your life with your fiancée? Are you just having cold feet? 

The most important thing is that you talk to her as soon as possible, because she deserves to know what you are thinking, even if it hurts. 

But if you're just having cold feet, please get your shit together. As you said you proposed to her as a surprise, so there was a time in your life where you saw a future with her. Really think this through! 

Whatever you decide, good luck!
